newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Bank Central Asia at center.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Bank Central Asia at center.

text.p: Bank Central Asia offered a US$150 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue to Asian debt markets on Thursday.

The issue has a final maturity of six years but can be put or called after three years. It pays a margin of 62.5 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate and an all-in return of 74 basis point to top-tier managers.
LTCB Asia is arranger and bookrunner for the deal. Chase Manhattan Asia, Commerz Southeast Asia, Sakura Merchant Bank and Sanwa International Finance are the other arrangers.

"The spread is reasonably acceptable, but a lot of banks are taking a wait-and-see approach regarding Indonesian issues because of the political problems," said a syndicate manager at a European bank.
Bank Central Asia is the largest private bank in Indonesia.
But others said the pricing would be tight even under the the best of circumstances in Indonesia.
"The Bank Central Asia issue looks tight not only compared with its last issue, but also compared with Bank Internasional Indonesia's deal from a few weeks back," said another banker.
In June 1995, Bank Central Asia brought a three-year FRCD that paid a margin of 70 basis points over LIBOR and an all-in return of 83.3 basis points.
Bank Internasional Indonesia last July launched a US$50 million FRCD that paid an all-in return of 96.5 basis points over LIBOR.
"BCA's deal last year at 83 went quite well, and I think that's because poeple were still betting on more Indonesian tightening," said the banker.

"We did have some tightening, but in light of having other comparable deals out there and with the BII transaction not doing at well at 96.5, the BCA deal just looks bad at any time of year," he said.
News of an unusual transaction emerged on Wednesday.
Strategic Portfolio Management, an open-ended investment company incorporated in Labuan, has launched a US$45 million floating rate note isssue, arranger Korea First announced.
Ssangyong Investment Securities is the equity subscriber of the issuer and will provide a letter of commitment.

The issue can be put if the gross asset value of the fund on any dealing day falls below 110 percent of the principal amount of and accrued interest on the outstanding notes and if Ssangyong fails to inject more capital to maintain collateralization of 120 percent.
The three-year FRN pays a margin of 90 basis points and an all-in return of 102 basis points.
Fujian Investment and Enterprise Corp was out with a US$22 million term loan via arranger Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank.

Looking ahead, bankers said more Philippines banks are in the market. Allied Bank reportedly is looking for US$100 million in three-year money, while Rizal Commercial Bank is seeking US$75 million for three years.
Merrill Lynch is expected to bring a deal for Philippines Commercial International Bank, possibly with a five-year tenor.
Metrobank currently is in the market with a five-year FRCD, the first Philippine bank deal with such a long tenor.

In other news, Hong Kong's Sino Land closed its US$400 million loan facility. Sino Land said the deal represents the first time it or any of its units have borrowed a substantial amount of funds that have not been secured by assets.
The company said that the unsecured deal has started a trend for the rest of the territory. Hong Kong's Kerry Properties is in the market now with an unsecured loan.

The US$100 million FRCD for China Merchants Bank has been allocated. The deal was oversubscribed nearly two-fold but not increased, arrangers Chase Manhattan Asia and Tokyo-Mitsubishi International (HK) said.
